chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn Samāʿah, from Ibn Ribāṭ, from Jārūd; or Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Sammāl, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Jārūd, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to me: “O Jārūd, they are advised but do not accept, and when they hear of something they call out with it, or when they are told something they spread it.”
I said to them: Delay the Maghrib a little, but they left it until the stars became intertwined. So now I perform it when the disk has set.”

key_terms.أَذَاعُوهُ: they publicized it or spread it openly
key_terms.اشْتَبَكَتِ النُّجُومُ: the stars became densely visible or intermingled in the sky
key_terms.بِالْمَغْرِبِ: with Maghrib salat, the sunset prayer
key_terms.سَقَطَ الْقُرْصُ: the sun’s disk disappeared below the horizon
key_terms.يُنْصَحُونَ: they are given sincere advice or counsel

ai.seo_question: When should Maghrib salat be performed according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام criticizing people who do not accept sincere counsel and who publicize whatever they hear. In the specific legal context of salat, it indicates that Maghrib should not be excessively delayed; rather, he states that he performs it when the sun’s disk has set.
